mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals labor market softening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two months signals a deflationary environment, which erodes corporate pricing power and profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage inflation and cost pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days under expansionary monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes when FEDFUNDS < 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.8% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.8% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% in the same month signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which increases earnings visibility and supports higher equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 1% AND HOUST monthly change > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered months.
